correctness.rationale: For the iid product-uniform null and nonzero integer frequencies, write D=n^-1 a^T H b with H the sample-centering projection. E|D|^2=tr(H)/n^2. Haar balance for each coordinate has only the within-mode pairing and, when frequencies agree up to sign, a crossed pairing with the all-equal overlap removed. Indeed, a singleton index cannot balance, so only a 2+2 split or all four indices equal is possible, even for harmonically related frequencies. A single crossing contracts to the off-diagonal square sum of H^2, (n-1)/n, before division by n^4. For the two double crossings let B=sum_ij H_ij^4; inclusion-exclusion gives respectively (n-1)^2-2(n-1)^2/n+B and (n-1)-2(n-1)^2/n+B, using tr(H^4)=n-1. These produce all four displayed covariance cases. There are PQ unordered reverse-sign pairs and 2PQ(P+Q-2) unordered pairs sharing exactly one absolute frequency, which gives the rectangular formula. If (P+Q)/n^2 tends to c, the variance/mean ratio tends to 1+2c. At n=2 the final two cases coincide; the introductory phrase 'four values' should be read as four cases, as explicitly qualified in the scope. value.rationale: The complete signed-pair covariance table provides an exact input to the variance of arbitrary finite weighted harmonic sums under a natural null and explains when independence-style fixed-grid variance estimates miss a macroscopic contribution. It identifies a dependence mechanism due to marginal frequency sharing, not merely a larger-grid numerical correction. No null distribution approximation or level guarantee is inferred.
